title: Add to apt
note: long thread tracking effort to get micro packaged for apt/Debian; eventually succeeded, micro entered official Debian repos and Ubuntu 20.04

title: Multiple cursor support
note: original multi-cursor feature request/implementation (2016-2017): landed as vim-multiple-cursors-style (Alt-n/p/c/x), not sublime/vscode word-expand-then-ctrl-d style; known bugs at merge time (cursor sync on backspace, cursor merging)

title: Use "Command" key on Mac instead of ctrl?
note: Recurring "why doesn't Cmd-C/Cmd-V work like other Mac editors" confusion, explained by the owner as an architectural limit rather than a bug: micro is terminal-based and only receives key events the terminal application chooses to forward, and on Mac the terminal reserves Cmd-key combos for its own keybindings (e.g. Cmd-Q to close the terminal, Cmd-T new tab), so Cmd events generally never reach micro at all — there is no code path in micro that could special-case Cmd even if desired. Cmd-V often appears to "work" only because the terminal's own paste binding sends the clipboard contents as a stream of ordinary character key events, not because micro sees a real Cmd-V event; Cmd-C does not work to copy because micro's selection state is internal to micro and the terminal has no way to know what's selected. Users wanting Cmd-based bindings must remap at the terminal-app or OS level (e.g. BetterTouchTool) to emit the Ctrl/character sequences micro can actually receive.

title: terminal entry not found
note: recurring tcell 'terminal entry not found' across TERM values (screen, kitty, cygwin, st); resolved by auto-generating db from infocmp via mkinfo, later built into micro directly, but edge cases persist

title: Support text editing shorcuts
note: early (2016) design origin of bindings.json: zyedidia adopted pscollins's suggestion for a JSON keybinding config instead of hardcoding Mac Cmd shortcuts (rejected per #19, Ctrl used instead); some requested bindings (Ctrl-Backspace/Delete, Alt-Delete) are impossible because terminals never send them as distinct key events

title: Soft Wrap
note: softwrap origin: zyedidia confirmed as planned (2016-04), then shipped as `set softwrap on` (2016-10); later a toggle command/keybinding was added in v2.0.15 via #3783 (toggle softwrap), enabling e.g. Alt-Z like VS Code

title: Delete a line
note: Long-running issue distinguishing delete (no clipboard side-effect) from cut (Ctrl-K, which overwrites the system buffer): no built-in delete-only-line action exists, but the durable workaround given by the owner and reaffirmed by other users is rebinding a key to the chained action "SelectLine,Delete" in bindings.json, e.g. {"CtrlK": "SelectLine,Delete"}, which also avoids the noticeable clipboard-sync delay over SSH with X11 forwarding. Known residual gap: the Alt-g keybinding help screen still shows the stock "^K Cut line" label even after such a rebind, since it reflects the default action name rather than the user's override.

title: copy paste doesn't work well
note: long-running copy/paste confusion thread; explains micro's clipboard model (internal/terminal/external, xclip/xsel dependency, ssh limitations), later improved with OSC52 terminal clipboard support

title: Auto completion
note: long thread on autocompletion; core added simple buffer-word autocomplete natively (2019) plus command/filename completion, but full language-aware autocomplete deferred to LSP plugins (see lsp-support)

title: Suggestion: tree view file browser sidebar
note: long debate on adding a file-tree/sidebar to core; community leaned toward keeping micro a lean editor (not IDE) and resolved via plugins (filetree-plugin, filemanager)

title: Word wrap
note: softwrap alone breaks mid-word; users must combine wordwrap+softwrap, a long-undiscovered setting pairing

title: Any plans for a Vi mode?
note: owner declined built-in vi/modal mode 2016 (closed, 'rather just use Vim'); recurring feature request since, workarounds are keybinding tweaks or third-party Lua plugins (micro-vi-plugin), never core

title: PuTTY Selection Issues
note: Long-closed issue diagnosed by owner zyedidia as a PuTTY bug, not a micro bug: PuTTY sends the wrong escape codes for Shift/Ctrl+arrow key combinations, breaking keyboard-driven selection (mouse selection is unaffected and works fine) — verified by comparing against KiTTY, a PuTTY fork that sends the correct codes and was recommended as a workaround at the time; a 2024 comment gives an actual PuTTY-side fix that avoids needing KiTTY: in PuTTY 0.79, under Terminal -> Keyboard, set "Shift/Ctrl/Alt with the arrow keys" to "xterm-style bitmap".

title: Show invisibles (whitespaces, tabs, newlines...)
note: long-running (2016-2026, 62 thumbs-up) 'show invisibles' request; eventually resolved by indentchar and the showchars option landed in #3760

title: How to copy to clipboard in SSH session (Linux)?
note: Long-running community thread on copying/pasting over SSH: owner zyedidia explains micro on a remote host cannot reach the local machine's clipboard, so the terminal emulator must do the copy (its own modifier+select) rather than micro; xclip/xsel on the remote host make ctrl-c/ctrl-v reach a local X server via ssh -X but add a large per-operation delay (xsel worse than xclip) and X11 mouse-selection auto-fills PRIMARY on every selection, causing multi-second freezes, so several users end up uninstalling them; the eventual clean fix is setting "clipboard": "terminal" together with a terminal that supports OSC 52 (e.g. Alacritty), and absent that, ctrl+shift+c/ctrl+shift+v (terminal-owned) vs ctrl+c/ctrl+v (micro-owned) is the workaround split to know, since Shift+select routes through the terminal instead of micro.

title: Can I install Micro Command Line Editor using APT Command on Ubuntu?
note: zyedidia (2020): avoid Ubuntu's apt package, it was compiled in debug mode (spurious log files) and lags; prefer Debian's own repo (buster-backports era, up-to-date) or the released deb/getmic.ro installer; Calinou notes distro repos freeze at release so apt users don't get new micro versions until the next OS release

title: Feature request: Add support for code folding
note: long-running feature-request wishlist for code folding, no maintainer ruling; real substance (if any) is in referenced PRs #1683/#2942, not here

title: Emacs/Vi keybindings / multi-key sequences
note: zyedidia declines a dedicated vim/emacs mode but commits (2020-08-04) to upgrading the keybinding system for key-sequences (Ctrl-x Ctrl-f style) on the keybindings branch, prioritized so vim/emacs bindings could later ship as plugins; PR #1299 prototyped multi-key JSON bindings; still unmerged/open as of 2025 with a community vi-mode Lua plugin attempt (micro-vi-plugin) instead

title: make normal selections by keyboard
note: Long-running closed issue: Shift+Up/Down often fail to extend selection (while Shift+Left/Right work) because many terminals/multiplexers (tmux, xfce4-terminal, Konsole, macOS Terminal.app) either don't send an escape sequence for those combos or intercept them as their own shortcuts (tab switching, line scroll); zyedidia's own workaround (cross-referenced from #983) is a bindings.json override using explicit CSI-sequence entries written as JSON unicode escapes (safe, unlike the raw hex escapes that broke #2950) for Select*/Move*/Word* actions, and setting TERM=xterm-256color helps in some tmux setups but not others; root cause was never tracked down by the maintainer.

title: Escape sequences written on mouse movement
note: long-running tcell mouse-mode bug: split/garbled SSH escape sequences leak into buffer/terminal, multiple partial fixes over 2017-2020, many duplicate issues cross-referenced

title: "No suitable screen available" when running 64-bit micro in windows 7
note: Long-standing Windows issue: micro exits immediately with "No suitable screen available" in some terminal setups (mintty/Cygwin/Babun, sometimes cmd/PowerShell). Root cause per community investigation: tcell (micro's terminal library) does not support termios on Windows and errors out in terminals like mintty that rely on it. Workarounds found: unset the TERM environment variable (a stray TERM=xterm or MICRO_TRUECOLOR=1 leftover triggers the failure on cmd/PowerShell) fixes it there but loses truecolor; for mintty specifically, running via `winpty micro` works except mouse input is then unsupported. No actual code fix landed in-thread; maintainer dmaluka later asked (2024) whether it's still reproduced on a recent version, unanswered as of the last update.

title: Selecting text does not work in standard Linux console
note: Owner zyedidia's fix for shift-arrow text selection (and ctrl/ctrl-shift-arrow) not working under the bare Linux console (TERM=linux): the console driver doesn't send those escape sequences at all, so it needed both a kmap remapping the relevant keycodes to custom escape sequences (a supplemental.kmap adapted from the tilde editor, loaded via loadkeys, one-time per boot not per login) and a matching change in micro itself to recognize those custom sequences under TERM=linux; setting TERM=xterm is a workaround that makes it work without the kmap but breaks other console apps that rely on TERM=linux behavior (e.g. mc's F3/F4), so it's not recommended. The instructions ended up documented on the project wiki.

title: copy does not work in SSH session
note: Recurring "copy doesn't reach my local clipboard over SSH" reports, with the owner's standing explanation: micro on the remote host has no access to the local clipboard at all, since it is the terminal (running locally) that owns the connection to the OS clipboard. Two real fixes exist, not one: (1) disable micro's own mouse handling (`set mouse off` or equivalently the `mouse` setting) so raw mouse selection is handled by the local terminal itself, which then owns Ctrl-Shift-C/Cmd-C copy — downside noted by a user: terminal-native selection can't scroll to grab text past the visible window, unlike micro's own selection; (2) set micro's `clipboard` option to `terminal` to use the OSC52 escape-sequence protocol, which lets micro ask the (OSC52-supporting) terminal to write to the local clipboard over the SSH connection without disabling micro's mouse support — documented in `> help copypaste`. A third, narrower workaround needs no config change at all: holding Shift while mouse-selecting (fn on Mac) bypasses the running application's mouse-reporting entirely for that one selection, letting the terminal's own copy shortcut (e.g. Ctrl-Shift-C in gnome-terminal) grab exactly what's visible on screen.

title: Keybindings mostly not working
note: Wide-ranging 2018 keybinding Q&A that pins down several durable facts about micro's terminal-dependent key handling: (1) Shift-Backspace is fundamentally indistinguishable from plain Backspace because most terminals send the identical escape sequence — inspect what a terminal actually sends with the `> raw` command; (2) Alt bindings are case-sensitive (Alt-g != Alt-G, the latter meaning Alt-Shift-g) while non-Alt letter bindings are not; (3) any key to enter command mode (default CtrlE) can be freely rebound by rebinding the `CommandMode` action in bindings.json, and likewise any command can be bound directly via the `command:<cmd>` prefix (puts it in the command bar and runs it) or `command-edit:<cmd>` (places it in the command bar for further editing without running) — these two prefixes were added directly in response to this issue; (4) command-mode text supports tab-completion of command names (type `vs`+Tab -> `vsplit`); (5) Mac Terminal.app and Alacritty are called out as poor for Alt/Shift+arrow combos because they emit Unicode chars instead of escape sequences for Alt, unlike iTerm2 (fixable there via Preferences->Profiles->Keys->Left option key->Esc+); (6) the xterm modifier-code convention micro follows: modifier digit 2=Shift, 3=Alt, 4=Shift+Alt, 5=Ctrl, 6=Shift+Ctrl, 7=Alt+Ctrl, 8=Shift+Alt+Ctrl, appended into sequences like `\x1b[1;<N>A/B/C/D` for arrows, vs plain `\x1b<char>` for Alt+letter — cited when helping alacritty maintainers add correct escape output. A `run <cmd>` command already existed for backgrounded shell commands distinct from interactive ShellMode (CtrlB); a request for an IDE-style persistent output pane went unimplemented in core (third-party attempt: sum01/cmdlog-micro, described as broken/pre-release).

title: Added autocomplete for Go, based on gocode, fixes #174
note: Go autocomplete via gocode PR, 2018-2021, abandoned; concludes LSP would be better approach

title: shift is not recognized in screen/tmux session
note: screen/tmux TERM lacks Shift-Arrow escape sequences in terminfo; owner's fix is mkinfo or TERM=xterm-256color, or raw bindings.json overrides — terminfo gap, not a tcell bug

title: [Feature Request] Add support for Language Server Protocol servers
note: long-running feature request for LSP client support; closed won't-do in favor of external micro-plugin-lsp

title: Allow find-next without pressing enter
note: long-standing (2018-2026) high-engagement request to streamline find/find-next: users repeatedly confused that Ctrl-N/Ctrl-G require pressing Enter first after Ctrl-F

title: Make space indent by default and tab as an option
note: Rejected feature request to default to space indentation instead of tabs. Owner's rationale for keeping tabs as the default: the tab key should insert a literal tab character by default, and options exist for exactly this kind of preference (tabstospaces in settings.json) rather than changing defaults and forcing a config-upgrade disruption on existing users; a contributor separately noted Go source itself conventionally uses tabs. For users who want automatic per-file indent-style detection (not just a fixed default), the recommended combo is enabling tabtospaces plus the third-party dmaluka/micro-detectindent plugin, since micro has no built-in auto-detection.

title: request:Transparent Background (i.e) same as terminal
note: Closed issue collecting the community's workarounds for a transparent (terminal-matching) background, since micro has no dedicated transparency option: omitting the background half of `color-link default "[fg],[bg]"` in a custom colorscheme falls back to the terminal's own background; any 16-color colorscheme (e.g. the built-in "simple") works because 16-color schemes don't hardcode an opaque bg; or explicitly set the bg to `#00000000` in a copied colorscheme file under ~/.config/micro/colorschemes for finer control.

title: [WSL] Copy doesn't work
note: WSL-specific clipboard failures; clip.exe/xclip shims, OSC52 support added, 'set clipboard terminal' workaround, same config-mode confusion as SSH cases

title: Added V syntax support
note: the owner rules that .v detects as V despite the conflict with Verilog, says he may reverse it because Verilog is more widely used, and notes users can set precedence themselves. Re-routed from no-signal: the ruling sits under forty comments of flamewar about whether V is a scam, and the pilot triager read the noise and called the thread empty — docs/ghmem-tail-sample.md adjudicates that call as wrong, and it is the miss the rubric was revised to catch.

title: Syntax highlighting with tree-sitter
note: tree-sitter integration proposal rejected for cgo dependency breaking cross-compilation (zyedidia); deferred to a possible future release rather than 2.0; recurring pure-Go preference from community; later WASM-compiled-grammar alternative floated (bartekpacia) with performance skepticism (anonyco), unresolved

title: Initial support for highlighting all search matches
note: Closed/superseded-by-#1762 PR that nonetheless carries the real design debate behind the `hlsearch` (highlight-all-search-matches) feature. Two architectures were weighed: (A) this PR's approach, extending pkg/highlight.Highlighter with a "custom pattern" overlay layer (AddCustomPattern/RemoveCustomPattern/highlightCustomMatches) reusing the syntax highlighter's match-storage machinery — rejected long-term because it couples custom highlighting to the syntax highlighter, making it harder to later swap in a different syntax engine (tree-sitter, #1466), and risks matches diverging from what FindNext finds; (B) the eventually-adopted #1762 approach, a LineArray-based per-line result cache computed via repeated FindNext calls. A naive "just search every visible line on every display call" alternative was measured and rejected: regex search is expensive enough (confirmed by CPU profiling) that doing it on every redraw made hlsearch the most battery-draining part of micro, which is why #1762 caches per-line results instead of recomputing them each frame. Also surfaced and fixed in this line of work: BufPane.HighlightCustomPattern lets Lua plugins highlight arbitrary regex patterns with colorscheme-group colors (independent feature, kept in the final implementation) and the default hlsearch style is an underline (owner's preference, for a "more subtle" look distinguishable from selection) rather than reversed colors, contrary to the author's own preference for a colored background — colorschemes can override via `color-link hlsearch "..."`.

title: New feature: Highlighting whitespace errors
note: Merged PR (dmaluka) adds two options, both off by default: hltaberrors highlights tab/space indentation errors using the tabstospaces setting as the criterion (tab chars flagged when tabstospaces is on, leading spaces flagged when it's off), and hltrailingws highlights trailing whitespace but suppresses the highlight on the line currently being typed until the cursor leaves it, so normal in-progress typing isn't flagged, only whitespace left behind after moving on.

title: Fix softwrap scrolling issues
note: Introduces internal/display/softwrap.go and the core softwrap data model still in use: SLoc{Line, Row} represents a vertical scroll position as a buffer line number plus a visual row (sub-line) within it, replacing plain int line numbers everywhere scrolling math is done (View.StartLine is now an SLoc). BufWindow.getRow(loc) computes which visual row a buffer.Loc falls in via width := w.Width - w.gutterOffset (minus scrollbar column) then util.StringWidth(...)/width — this is the concrete site where wrapping width is derived from live pane geometry rather than any setting, confirming there is no config knob to intercept here without patching this function. getRowCount(line) is getRow of the line's last character + 1, i.e. how many visual rows a given buffer line occupies when wrapped. Scroll(s, n)/Diff(s1, s2) do SLoc-aware arithmetic (scrollUp/scrollDown/diff helpers) so page-up/down, centering, and Relocate work correctly across wrapped lines; before this PR these operations used plain buffer-line arithmetic and broke under softwrap (issues #632, #1657). BufWindow.Bottomline() was removed as fundamentally broken under softwrap and replaced by `w.Scroll(v.StartLine, height-1)`. A noted still-open edge case: getRow's width-based row computation "doesn't work quite correctly if there is an incomplete tab or wide character at the end of a row" (#1979). Follow-on softwrap work (cursor up/down within a wrapped line, word wrapping) continued in PR #2076.

title: CTRL + Backspace to remove previous word.
note: terminal-dependent Backspace vs Backspace2 encoding for Ctrl-Backspace; zyedidia: OldBackspace binding is the (confusingly undocumented) fix, terminals rarely differ Backspace/Backspace2 so micro treats them as equivalents by default; repeated newcomer requests through 2026 to document OldBackspace in keybindings.md, never actioned

title: syntax highlighting missing for conf and config files
note: Open issue tracking the long-standing lack of built-in .conf/.cfg syntax highlighting: neitsab found micro used to highlight conf files until commit 975e78d9c0 deliberately removed the conf syntax definition (too many conflicts with other filetypes' detection); current workarounds are a user-authored ~/.config/micro/syntax/conf.yaml, or mapping "*.conf" to filetype "ini" via settings.json, or (per Andriamanitra) the default.yaml fallback mechanism added in #2933, which ships with no ini/conf rules out of the box so users must supply their own default.yaml; six other issues (#2466, #3401, #3751, #4004, #4021) are cross-referenced duplicates of the same request.

title: Ctrl-v to paste not working
note: Maintainer zyedidia explains the clipboard option: with clipboard=internal (the default), micro never touches the system clipboard, so ctrl-c/ctrl-v inside micro only round-trip through micro's own buffer while the terminal's own paste (e.g. cmd-v/right-click) still delivers the OS clipboard, producing the confusing symptom of ctrl-v pasting stale cut text instead of what was just copied; the fix on macOS is to set clipboard to external, and on WSL the system clipboard needs an xclip-shim workaround (e.g. Konfekt/xclip-xsel-WSL) since there's no X server.

title: Clipboard from SSH
note: SSH clipboard config confusion: terminal/external modes, mouse setting interactions, X11 forwarding workarounds

title: scrolling performance very slow (scrolling)
note: long-running open issue: holding an arrow key to scroll keeps scrolling for seconds after release, on weak/ARM hardware and after macOS window resize; tracked as a 'major' issue via #2970, root causes not fixed but two known CPU hotspots identified during scroll redraws: tcell's CanDisplay() (#3227) and repeated buf.Settings map lookups (#3228); one report traces it to TERM=vt100 vs xterm

title: Option for setting length of lines
note: Long-requested feature: soft-wrap at a fixed column (not the pane's right edge), useful for prose/writing workflows; existing workaround from dmaluka is a dummy left-hand vertical split resized (via ResizePane, mouse drag, or a small init.lua/plugin) so the working pane's width equals the desired wrap column, but this is fragile (percentage-based ResizePane needed because terminal startup geometry races with micro's own startup resize, and pre-#1800-fix versions call onBufPaneOpen before the pane is fully initialized) and the requester ultimately found the extra split more distracting than the long lines it fixed, preferring a real margin/column option over a workaround pane. The repo's own account (ddaanet) posted a concrete design settled and later implemented as issue #4142: a `softwrapcolumn` integer common option, default 0 (off, current behavior), wraps at that column when >0 and softwrap is on, clamped to pane width so a narrow pane still wraps at its edge, deliberately kept orthogonal to both `wordwrap` and `colorcolumn` (colorcolumn is a visual guide only and coupling it to wrapping would surprise people who set it for the ruler alone), with continuation rows still starting at column 0 so cursor/loc mapping is untouched.

title: Ctrl-c (copy) does not work
note: Long-running open issue on Ctrl-C not copying: maintainer dmaluka rules "this is not a bug in micro, this is a terminal emulator issue" — a terminal either consumes Ctrl-C itself (as its own copy-to-clipboard shortcut) or passes it through to the running application, never both, so when the terminal consumes it micro never receives the byte at all (diagnosable by running micro's `raw` command and checking whether pressing Ctrl-C prints anything); he doubts any terminal implements a mode-aware split (consume in command-line mode, pass through in full-screen/application mode) though kitty's `send_text application` looked promising and didn't pan out when tried; separately, several commenters report `set clipboard terminal`/`set clipboard external` (the latter needing xclip/wl-copy installed) as the fix for their case, so the terminal-consumes-the-shortcut explanation is not the only cause in this thread.

title: Consider adding flatpak packages and publishing to flathub
note: Micro was published to Flathub as io.github.zyedidia.micro (accepted 2023-04) after several appdata/metainfo.xml fixes (PRs #2792, #2793, #2796, #2803, the last adding type="desktop-application" so it would actually appear in the store rather than just being installable). Practical flatpak-specific facts users hit afterward: config lives at ~/.var/app/io.github.zyedidia.micro/config/micro, not the native ~/.config/micro (both can exist simultaneously with different contents if the native binary was also run); flatpaks cannot install an executable onto $PATH, so running it as plain `micro` requires a shell alias/function wrapping `flatpak run io.github.zyedidia.micro`, and the same command string is what to put in $EDITOR. As of the last comment (2024-12) the flathub listing was still unverified (no response on verification request), and a separate "flathub package out of date" issue (#2980) exists as staleness follow-up.

title: Blank screen / hang on startup
note: long-running open issue: micro hangs blank on startup, root-caused to wl-clipboard hanging when reading/writing an empty clipboard (upstream wl-clipboard bug, dup of #2577/#3078/#4079); workarounds are settings.json clipboard:terminal or clipboard:internal, or switching to wl-clipboard-rs

title: Implemented sub-word cursor movement
note: maintainer dmaluka pushes back on masmu's SubWord PR: renames IsNonAlphaNumeric->IsNonWordChar, proposes IsSubwordDelimiter, debates WordRight/Left inconsistency vs SubWord; merged 2024-05-21, follow-up trailing-whitespace bug spun into #3321

title: Fix: Syntax highlighting for various issues
note: PR #2810 (merged): fixes 13 separate syntax-highlighting bugs (bash, PHP, JS, Ruby, C/C++, etc.) whose root cause was the highlighter incorrectly gating regex matches containing literal ^ or $ characters behind a canMatchStart/canMatchEnd flag pair meant to represent line-start/line-end anchors -- but Go regexp/RE2 treats ^ and $ inside a pattern as matching every line-tokenized chunk passed to it (not just the true first/last line), so the gating silently dropped valid rule matches on later lines. JoeKar traced this via debug logging and screenshot comparisons against Vim/Emacs/Neovim, and the fix removes the start/end tracking entirely rather than trying to special-case it. zyedidia (owner) accepted the tradeoff of "compromising some incremental highlight performance" since most files are not huge, and noted the syntax highlighting system needs a full rework (linking the stalled github.com/zyedidia/flare project) that only lacked time/language files -- a separate, earlier rework attempt than the one tracked in [[highlighter-performance]].

title: Improve file detection with signature check capabilities
note: PR adding multi-line signature/header-based filetype detection (detectlimit option, filename-check precedence over header regex, tie-break among ambiguous matches by scanning body for a signature); rejected folding detectindent plugin into this same pass (kept as separate plugin, not core)

title: options: Add `truecolor` to control the mode
note: new truecolor option (auto/on/off) replaces MICRO_TRUECOLOR env var; key finding: tcell already autodetects truecolor by default and micro was deliberately overriding it off, so the PR mostly exposes existing tcell behavior rather than adding new capability; default kept off initially for compat, later changed to auto (breaking change accepted after ~2 years of discussion); colorscheme tc/16-suffix naming inconsistencies noted as a follow-on problem

title: options: add `matchbracestyle`
note: matchbracestyle enum (underline/highlight) chosen over a boolean for future generic option-toggling (#2086); usability bug found+fixed where reverse-color highlight collided with cursor rendering; design simplified to only match braces the cursor sits directly on, dropping the confusing 'brace to the left' case

title: syntax: Provide default.yaml as fallback definition
note: adds runtime/syntax/default.yaml as filetype:unknown fallback (mail/URL rules only, kept minimal per reviewer pushback on config-file-specific rules); refactors UpdateRules() into findRuntimeSyntaxDef/findRealRuntimeSyntaxDef helpers

title: Binding raw escape sequences doesn't work
note: Closed issue: bindings.json can't bind raw terminal escape sequences like \x1bOC/\x1bOD (e.g. MobaXterm's CtrlShiftLeft/Right) because JSON string literals reject arbitrary \xHH escapes, producing "invalid character 'x' in string escape code"; duplicate of the same limitation reported earlier in #1863. JoeKar (maintainer) began checking whether bindings.go's handling of a 0x1b-prefixed sequence (per keybindings.md's own description of terminal escape events) is sufficient to support such bindings some other way.

title: [Request & Discussion] Extended rights for volunteers to help supporting your `micro` project
note: single-maintainer bottleneck (zyedidia) resolved 2024-03: JoeKar+dmaluka added as maintainers with merge rights; core deps migrated to micro-editor org, main repo migration still pending

title: command: Add capability to use relative numbers in goto
note: PR #2985 added +/- relative line prefixes to 'goto', breaking the existing nano-style 'goto -N' (from end of file, #1691); resolved with '~' reserved for from-end jumps and +/- for relative, merged 2023-11, but reverted 2024-03-17 by dmaluka after zoomosis reported the #1691 regression — reopened #2897 for community discussion of a separate relativegoto/jump command instead

title: highlighter: Change the parsing approach to significantly improve performance
note: long-running (2024-2026) architectural rewrite of the highlighter's parsing approach for perf; exponential-time regions bug found, byte-vs-rune line storage tension spun off to #3149, converted back to draft 2025-04-26 for being too hard to follow; both PR authors became maintainers mid-thread

title: plugin: formatter: Add plugin to format files
note: Closed PR proposing a built-in formatter plugin; the review thread renders to roughly 42KB, past what this pass could load in full, so this verdict rests only on the visible opening exchange — JoeKar questioning whether a separate enable option is needed at all since activating the plugin already implies the functionality — which is an unresolved single question, not a settled convention or maintainer ruling, so nothing citable was actually captured.

title: buffer: Add proper lock mechanism to lock the full `LineArray` instead of single lines
note: Merged PR fixing a real race between the async highlighter goroutine and main-goroutine buffer edits (lines freed mid-highlight caused sporadic macOS CI failures/deadlocks); design settled through review (dmaluka): drop the abandoned per-line NoLock/Lock function-duplication approach in favor of a single whole-LineArray mutex plus keeping the existing per-line locks for state/match (so displayBuffer only waits on one line's lock, not the whole array), have HighlightStates/HighlightMatches/ReHighlightStates lock-check-unlock per iteration (`for i:=0;;i++ { input.Lock(); if i>=input.LinesNum(){Unlock();break}; ...; input.Unlock() }`) so the highlighter itself validates the current line count under lock rather than trusting a stale LinesNum() snapshot, and add explicit Buffer.Lock()/Unlock() around Retab's raw append into `b.lines[i].data` (noted as separately buggy - bypasses EventHandler so retab can't be undone - but deferred as a distinct issue); benchmarking showed no real throughput cost from the fix itself, the apparent 10x slowdown was from re-enabling InitRuntimeFiles(false) in the test, not the locking.

title: docs: Improve plugin documentation
note: Merged docs PR rewriting runtime/help/plugins.md; maintainer dmaluka's review establishes that plugin help docs must stay readable as plain text inside micro, not just as rendered markdown, and pushed back on a footnote-style link reference for being confusing under that constraint; he also corrected a claim that plugins are merely unlikely to load syntax header files, noting RTSyntaxHeader is not exported to Lua so they cannot do so at all, and asked for consistent indentation on function-description continuation lines.

title: action: Stop processing chained actions/commands in the moment the current `Pane` is not a `BufPane` (fix crash)
note: Fixed a crash where BufMapEvent's chained-action loop kept calling execAction after the current pane changed to a non-BufPane (TermPane/InfoPane), by breaking when CurPane() returns nil; CurPane() stays typed *action.BufPane for Lua/plugin-API stability rather than becoming the generic Pane interface, since gopher-luar has no Go type-assertion support for plugins to narrow it back down. Maintainers noted two real remaining gaps this PR does not close: chained keybindings still silently stop rather than actually working once they hit a non-buf pane (#2307, #2288 crashes are fixed but the bindings still don't do what the user wanted), and onAction/preAction callbacks are still unsupported for non-buf panes (#2677). The success/innerSuccess return-value plumbing in bufAction was found to be unused except by InfoPane's DoKeyEvent, which is untangled separately in PR #3267.

title: save: Perform write process safe
note: merged PR making save() atomic: temp-file+rename with overwrite fallback, symlink resolution, backup reuse, rejects FIFOs/device files/irregular files

title: Changing syntax behavior for single quote to allow binary and hex literal separator
note: C++14/C23 digit-separator (') literal highlighting fix: applied to cpp.yaml only (not c.yaml, performance tradeoff decided by dmaluka), workaround error regex pending #3127 syntax-region rewrite (TODO to revert), later caused a regression (enum-value digits highlighted as numbers) fixed by follow-on PRs #3870/#3891/#3905

title: Added Syntax Highlighting for nftables-firewall config file
note: backfilled note, no reason was recorded at routing time: newcomer's nftables syntax file, reviewed by a contributor who explicitly disclaims knowing nftables or syntax highlighting well enough to review it. The thread is yaml corrections against one language file and carries no decision, rationale, or contested position — a clean no-signal.

title: nightly: Use GitHub Actions for scheduled builds
note: migrated nightly builds from zyedidia's manual/local process to GitHub Actions (cross-compile.sh rewritten with per-platform artifact helper, sha256 checksums, softprops/action-gh-release); needed GITHUB_TOKEN read/write workflow permissions (default changed Feb 2023), zyedidia disabled the old CI after confirming; follow-up PR #3418 fixed nightly asset naming so updates don't just accumulate old version-named files

title: Improve and unify `CopyLine`, `CutLine`, `DeleteLine`, `DuplicateLine` actions
note: PR #3335 (merged): unifies CopyLine/CutLine/DeleteLine/DuplicateLine to respect multi-line selections (previously only acted on the cursor's current line) and adds a new Duplicate action for selection-only duplication; default keybindings changed to action|actionLine pairs (e.g. Ctrl-c: Copy|CopyLine) to preserve old defaults. Discussion also revisits CutLine's append-to-clipboard (freshClip) behavior: the buggy, never-working lastCutTime 10-second reset is removed, and after debating renames (ClipLine, CutLineAppend, CutAndClipLine) the maintainers keep CutLine's existing append semantics as-is rather than splitting into a separate action, just documenting it and pointing users to CopyLine,DeleteLine for the non-appending alternative.

title: Rework `filetype` change, `reload` command and `autosave`
note: maintainer deep-dive (JoeKar+dmaluka) reworking 'reload'/'set filetype'/autosave: reload must skip volatile settings, autosave rearchitected to persistent goroutine w/ retime channel (fixed goroutine leak), filetype-triggered reinit caused duplicate errors/crashes; broke plugins that write buf.Settings directly instead of SetOptionNative

title: workflows: General improvements
note: Merged PR debugging why tools/build-version.go (git describe --tags-based version string, used by both make and CI) fell back to "0.0.0-unknown" in GitHub Actions: root cause was actions/checkout's default shallow clone giving `git describe --tags` nothing to find, fixed by adding `fetch-depth: 0` and `fetch-tags: true` to the checkout step in both nightly.yaml and test.yaml (superseding the old build-version.go-internal `git fetch --tags` fallback, which was also flagged as an unwanted side effect for a version-reporting tool to have, and which can fail outright in the upstream repo because the nightly workflow's own force-updated "nightly" tag causes `git fetch --tags` to reject as "would clobber existing tag"); also added `workflow_dispatch` to nightly.yaml so it can be tested on demand instead of waiting for the daily cron, and added stderr-printing `log.Printf` calls around each semver parse/exec fallback in build-version.go so future version-string failures are diagnosable instead of silent.

title: Fixing comment plugin not using user settings when overriding default setting
note: comment.lua commenttype override was clobbered on filetype change; fix (JoeKar) introduces comment.type via RegisterCommonOption plus DoSetOptionNative -- the key distinction dmaluka documents is that SetOptionNative marks an option as locally-overridden (survives reload/filetype change) while DoSetOptionNative just sets the buffer value without that mark, so per-filetype computed defaults must use DoSetOptionNative or they freeze at first value; commenttype renamed to comment.type with backward-compat alias kept permanently (dmaluka: no noisy runtime warning, just a doc note it may be deprecated later); recurring maintainer ask for one-functional-change-per-commit history for bisectability

title: add actions CursorToViewTop, CursorToViewCenter, CursorToViewBottom
note: new CursorToView{Top,Center,Bottom} actions to reposition cursor within the current view without scrolling; design settled through iteration: must account for soft-wrapped lines (SLoc not just line number) when checking if cursor is in view, scrollmargin is suppressed at buffer start/end to avoid unexpected jumps (deliberate, not a bug), multicursor state must be cleared via Buf.ClearCursors() before the move (RemoveAllMultiCursors() reorders badly since it itself calls Relocate()); explicitly NOT meant to fix PageUp/PageDown's cursor-jumps-to-top behavior — that's deferred to a separate action/behavior-change discussion (nano-style paging, referencing #1808) so as not to break existing user expectations by changing CursorPageUp/Down semantics directly

title: Nftables improvements
note: Merged PR adding/refining the nftables.yaml syntax-highlighting file; the whole thread is routine line-by-line regex/style nitpicking specific to that one filetype (operator grouping, hex-vs-decimal number matching, indentation consistency, filename-detection regex) with no generalizable rule about micro's syntax-highlighting mechanism itself, just cleanup of a stalled contributor's syntax file before merge.

title: implement nano-like page up/page down functionality
note: Merged PR reworks CursorPageUp/Down (and SelectPageUp/Down) to behave nano/vim-like: instead of jumping a full view-height and losing place, they scroll by (view height - pageoverlap) while moving the cursor the same amount, keeping a fixed line-overlap between pages; adds the new "pageoverlap" setting (default 2, validated non-negative) rather than reusing scrollmargin, because maintainer dmaluka argued scrollmargin (used while slow-scrolling) and page overlap are conceptually different and a user may want one at zero while keeping the other. Multi-cursor correctness required guarding the view-scroll calls with h.Cursor.Num==0 so the view is scrolled only once per keypress, not once per cursor (the naive multi-cursor version scrolled the view far away since ScrollUp/Down and MoveCursorUp/Down were both called per-cursor via MultiActions). The remaining scrollmargin-during-paging interaction is intentional and kept via the existing h.Relocate() call: paging respects scrollmargin the same way normal cursor movement does, matching vim's scrolloff behavior, rather than adding a fancier direction-aware relocate.

title: Added support for multi-cursor comments to the comment plugin
note: Multi-cursor support for the comment plugin: reworked toggleCommentSelection to operate over a table of lines gathered from all cursors rather than a single start/end range, with cursor positions restored via per-cursor displacement afterward; maintainer JoeKar also stated a position against a start-of-line/unindented comment placement option (issue #2282), preferring the current indented alignment as the default, and pushed for rebase-not-merge history hygiene on long-lived PRs.

title: Paste into Window micro misformats the pasted values
note: Issue #3571 (open, long-running since 2024-12): pasting on Windows Terminal causes cascading auto-indent ('staircase' effect) because Windows Terminal intercepts Ctrl-v itself and forwards pasted text to micro as individual key events rather than as a bracketed paste (EventPaste), so autoindent applies per character as if typed. Root cause (confirmed 2026-01 by JoeKar via raw-input tracing and comparing against Microsoft's edit and Windows Terminal source) is that micro/tcell's legacy Windows console backend never requests ENABLE_VIRTUAL_TERMINAL_INPUT, so Windows Terminal never emits bracketed-paste sequences to it. Workarounds in the thread: rebind Paste to a non-intercepted key (e.g. Alt-v), or wrap Ctrl-v as 'setlocal autoindent off,Paste,setlocal autoindent on'. Confirmed fixed 2026-06/07 on the tcell/v3 branch, which does negotiate bracketed paste on Windows (verified working by both JoeKar and the reporter, with a noted redraw glitch on paste-over-selection and a status-bar PASTE indicator side effect).

title: match beginning and end of line correctly
note: FindNext/ReplaceRegex matched ^/$/\b against the search *range* boundaries, not real line start/end, causing false matches mid-line; fixed by padding the regex with a required leading/trailing '.' (non-capturing group) only on the first/last line of the range, then trimming that padding rune back out of the match; settled on compiling the padded variant lazily per line rather than precompiling all 4 combinations; ReplaceRegex needed the same fix via a new findAll() helper, replacing per-line ReplaceAllFunc with per-match deltas processed in reverse

title: Removing the ability for plugins to modify settings.json and bindings.json. Adding an option to reject plugins to bind keys.
note: PR #3618 (merged): plugins can no longer write settings.json/bindings.json directly (TryBindKeyPlug/SetGlobalOptionPlug set values without persisting to file); new lockbindings option (default false) lets users block plugins from binding keys at all, to guard against accidental irreversible actions from unreviewed keybinds.

title: statusline: Provide `overwrite` mode indicator
note: adds overwrite-mode indicator to statusline; state moved to Buffer (not BufPane/Cursor) matching the LastSearch/HighlightSearch precedent so it works correctly per-bufpane even when sharing a buffer; long bikeshed over indicator text (ins/ovr/ovwr/overwrite) settled on fixed-width [ovwr] to avoid statusline resize flicker; made mutually exclusive with [ro] since overwrite is meaningless on a readonly buffer

title: enhance search API
note: extensive API design negotiation: RegexpGroup/RegexpSearch/RegexpData naming, submatch function shape, start>end semantics rejected as 'too smart', ReplaceAll replaces ReplaceRegex, commit-organization expectations for large PRs

title: buffer: Fix `ReloadSettings(true)` for volatile `filetype`
note: Merged PR splitting InitLocalSettings into UpdatePathGlobLocals (path globs, checked on every reload) and UpdateFileTypeLocals (ft: block, checked only when filetype resolves) so ReloadSettings(true) fires onBufferOptionChanged/OptionCallback when filetype actually changes; review caught a glob-locals regression (only worked after `> reload`), a crash from `ft:` settings.json entries, and settled that filetype changes need SetOptionNative-style callback firing via a new doCallbacks helper shared by DoSetOptionNative.

title: Fix unable to perform proportional resize caused by chained parents after quiting a nested VSplit inside a HSplit
note: Merged core fix: micro's tab layout is a tree of Type/Type Node children (visualized via bp:Tab():String()), and quitting a nested pane inside e.g. HSplit->VSplit->HSplit can leave a "chained parent" — a node with a single child left over from the unsplit — that isn't collapsed, so a later resize call hits the wrong parent and proportional resize degrades (e.g. 50/25/25 instead of an even 33/33/33 across three HSplits); the fix simplifies/collapses the tree on unsplit so chained single-child parents don't survive to confuse later resize calculations.

title: Skip save on `open` or `term` command if buffer is shared
note: PR generalizes save-before-close prompt (open/term/quit) into closePrompt, and adds Buffer.Shared() to skip the prompt when another buffer already has the file open (matches #3559 for quit); review exposed that onSave/onSaveAs/preSave firing rules are undocumented and inconsistent across Save/SaveAs/quit-prompt paths (also seen in #3550, #3689) — maintainers decided documenting the mess is more realistic than unifying it

title: Overlays, example overlay plugins
note: Open draft PR (glupi-borna) implementing the overlay/popup-layer API following the design sketched in a comment on issue #3465: keeps the Go-side surface minimal, deliberately pushing composition complexity to the plugin side for flexibility, and ships two example plugins (a cursor-adjacent autocomplete overlay and a search/palette widget) plus a more involved quickmenu input-box example, all built around an immediate-mode style for handling overlay events since proper event handling in plugin code was found to be non-trivial to get right; author explicitly does not want the example plugins to become default, they exist only to demonstrate the API in this draft.

title: Adding indenttabchar, indentspacechar and spacechar options
note: merged: added indenttabchar/indentspacechar/spacechar, deprecating indentchar; design debate over naming vs repurposing indentchar, tabsize-relative highlighting confusion, and whether indent chars should respect tabstospaces (dropped that check); author flagged a follow-up PR adding eol/inv/wrap char options

title: micro: Handle +/text search text from args
note: Added vim-style `+/REGEX` CLI arg support (e.g. `micro +/imem_size +623 file.c`) alongside the existing `+LINE[:COL]`, landing as a new internal/buffer.Command{StartCursor, SearchRegex, SearchAfterStart} struct that replaces the old NewBufferFromFileAtLoc/NewBufferFromStringAtLoc cursor-only API (now NewBufferFromFileWithCommand/NewBufferFromStringWithCommand) — deliberately generalized past just the CLI since dmaluka noted the same "command" concept applies to vim/vi/ed/sed-style runtime use later. SearchAfterStart (true when +/REGEX appears after +LINE:COL in argv) replaces an earlier CommandOrder enum with a plain bool. Regex safety was scoped explicitly: only constant regex fragments used internally are compiled with regexp.MustCompile, while the actual user-supplied search text reuses the existing (already-crash-prone per #3700, the `+/\Q` panic) FindNext search path rather than adding a new unguarded MustCompile on user input. A real bug caught in review: forgetting to update the cursor's OrigSelection alongside CurSelection when a `+/TEXT` match sets the initial selection, which broke Shift+Right/Shift+Down extension after opening with a search.

title: Add toggle & togglelocal command
note: re-routed from no-signal: the review is mostly line-level nits, except dmaluka's "we can just use SetGlobalOptionNative(), no point converting to string just to convert it back" — which is the distinction this topic exists for. The calibration called this the revised rubric's one residual miss and genuinely fuzzy; on the content test rather than the settledness test, it routes.

title: Enhance Tab Bar
note: re-routed from no-signal: dmaluka's review is substantial design guidance, and that is institutional knowledge whether or not the PR lands — t.release alone cannot tell a drag from a click that began off the tabbar, so a separate dragging field is wanted, and TabMoveCmd should not be reused for the move. The earlier verdict asked whether the thread had concluded, which is the wrong test; when the thread moves, the next sync-triage-synthesize run rewrites the topic doc.

title: backup+util: Prevent too long backup file names with hashing + resolve file
note: long paths overflow backup/serialized-buffer filenames; explored base64/deflate/LUT-of-hashes before settling on: keep URL-encoding as happy path, but when escaped path+suffix exceeds 255 chars, fall back to md5(path) as filename plus a sibling {hash}.path file holding the original path (DetermineEscapePath returns (name, resolveName)); a late review found the fallback path was written outside the backup dir (missing filepath.Join) before merge

title: Adding missing file closes
note: Merged PR fixing leaked file handles on Windows (unclosed files blocked git branch switches) by adding missing file.Close() calls in safeWrite()/ReOpen() error paths, and refactoring the backup step into a new writeBackup() helper; review (dmaluka, JoeKar) reaffirmed the deliberate ordering from #3273 that forceKeepBackup must stay false until the backup write actually succeeds, so a failed write/close leaves the backup around for retry rather than silently discarding it, and flagged that the new code path still leaves forceKeepBackup=true if safeWrite's file.Close() itself errors.

title: Adding the ability to differentiate builtin plugins when listing
note: Merged PR renames Plugin.Default to Builtin (JoeKar: "Builtin is somehow more self explaining... wouldn't require the additional comment") and changes `-plugin list` to print "(built-in)" instead of a version for bundled plugins, since their bundled version never gets updated and so is useless, while still showing a real version if the user's own ~/.config/micro/plug copy overrides a built-in one and its Builtin flag isn't set; initlua is deliberately excluded from Builtin (dmaluka: "it doesn't come with micro, it is created by the user") and printed bare with no version/suffix at all; a parenthesization bug (`|| p.Name == "initlua"` sitting outside the enclosing condition) made every successful `-plugin remove` print "Default plugins cannot be removed" even though removal still succeeded via `continue`, fixed alongside renaming the message to name the specific built-in plugin.

title: Update man page + change `[FILE]:LINE:COL` to `FILE[:LINE:COL]` in `micro -help`
note: Man-page/-help rewrite surfaced (dmaluka, in review) micro's actual CLI cursor-position semantics: `FILE:LINE[:COL]` only takes effect if the `parsecursor` option is enabled, while `+LINE[:COL]` always works regardless of that option but is a single argument applied to every file opened on the command line rather than per-file; the two forms are mutually exclusive and `+LINE[:COL]` takes priority, so `micro foo:10 bar +20` opens both `foo` and `bar` at line 20, not `foo` at 10; if several `+LINE[:COL]` args are given only the last is applied; and `+LINE[:COL]` is still honored even with no file argument, opening an unnamed empty buffer with the cursor at that (nonexistent) line/column.

title: Include --options-with-hyphens in statement regex
note: Long discussion arriving at the final runtime/syntax/sh.yaml option-highlighting regex: settled on (\s|^)(-[A-Za-z0-9]+|--[A-Za-z0-9][\w-]*|--(\s|$)) after debating whether to match --a single-letter long opts (yes, getopt_long allows them, GNU truncation like --v for --version is real), whether to highlight bare -- (yes, marks end-of-options), the \s+ prefix missing line-continuation cases (foo \ \n --bar), and accepting --------- as a known false positive since Go regexp lacks lookahead/lookbehind for a cleaner fix.

title: quick fix for #3700
note: Fixes the #3700 crash where a search regex containing `\Q` without a closing `\E` (e.g. bare `\Q`) panicked instead of erroring, by making internal/buffer/search.go's findLineParams surface regexp.Compile errors instead of relying on regexp.MustCompile on padded patterns; error messages now reach the user (previously swallowed) via a related actions.go fix making `err != nil` and `found` mutually exclusive branches. Per Go maintainer confirmation (golang/go#76424) `\Q` without `\E` is actually valid regex syntax meaning "quote to end of string", so the fix auto-corrects it by re-compiling with a trailing `\E` appended and using that if it succeeds, rather than rejecting it as an error — this recovery only runs when padMode is nonzero (i.e. actually needed) to avoid extra compiles per line. The same regex validation was found to need consistent handling in the `replace` command path too (ReplaceRegex could still crash pre-fix); it turned out already covered because both search and replace funnel through findLineParams.

title: Fixing missing case for handling root node for splitting
note: Merged fix for the pane-split Node tree's root-node handling (fixes crash issue #3980): the root node was identified by Kind==STUndef, but that sentinel became stale after the first split (root's Kind gets set to STVert/STHoriz and never reset), so later unsplit/quit logic misbehaved; the agreed fix identifies the root structurally via node.parent==nil instead, with flatten() given a special case for the root (copies the sole remaining child's fields into place, keeping parent nil) and STUndef is reset only when the flattened root ends up with zero children (i.e. truly back to the single-pane initial state) rather than whenever it becomes root — getting this wrong caused two follow-up crashes (nil pointer dereference on unsplit, and wrong resize when the intermediate node being flattened away had multiple grandchildren); String() debug output prints "-"/"|" by Kind rather than a special "/" for root, since a root with children is otherwise structurally the same as any other split node.

title: buffer: Store potential resolved symlinks as `AbsPath`
note: Merged PR fixing SharedBuffer identity for the same file opened via different symlinks (so undo history etc is correctly shared) by adding util.ResolvePath(), replacing plain filepath.Abs() calls in NewBuffer/saveToFile; extensive review settled several subtleties: must resolve every path component (not just the final file) since any intermediate symlink or the CWD itself can be a symlink, must resolve relative-to-absolute at each iteration since an intermediate symlink target can itself be relative, and for a not-yet-existing file (new/unsaved) ResolvePath walks up via filepath.Dir/EvalSymlinks until it finds an existing ancestor then rejoins the non-existent remainder so dir/file and dir1/file (dir1 -> dir) still resolve to the same absolute path; separately settled that when two symlinks/paths reach the same file, the statusline keeps showing whichever name was opened first ("first wins", deliberately not resolved like vim first appeared to do), and that Buffer.Fini() should only Serialize()/CancelBackup() when closing the last (non-shared) instance of a buffer, since each serialize just overwrites the previous cursor-position record. TOCTOU on the resolved path was acknowledged but explicitly left unaddressed - micro doesn't hold a file handle across a buffer's lifetime.

title: config.SetGlobalOption no longer allows writing to settings.json
note: Issue #4041 (open): pushback against PR #3618's removal of plugin settings.json writes, from a user whose plugins (chromakeys, miscutils) relied on SetGlobalOption persisting. Long, heated debate over whether write-protection should be unconditional or configurable, whether micro's JSON5 support is 'real' if writes discard comments/formatting, and alternatives (separate plugin-owned config files, an in-place JSON patcher, a SetGlobalOptionAndSave action, a whitelist of trusted plugins). Maintainers (dmaluka, JoeKar, Neko-Box-Coder) converge on a single extensible string-valued option `writesettings` (comma-separated keywords, e.g. `set`, `plugins`) controlling which write paths (the `set`/`bind` commands vs. plugin calls) persist to settings.json/bindings.json, defaulting to `set` only (today's post-#3618 behavior: plugins never write) — rejecting a per-plugin whitelist and a combined set+plugins boolean as over-engineering. Landed via #4046 and #4055 (both close this issue).

title: fix sudo TTY race and terminal state corruption
note: fixes #4050: concurrent sudo dd processes (truncate+write) raced on TCGETS2/TCSETS2, breaking sudo-rs; dmaluka traces the truncate-via-separate-dd design back to PR #3814/#3807 (need backup before truncate for safe sudo writes) and the eventual fix reorders safeWrite() to backup before openFile() for the sudo path (JoeKar's patch, adopted), returning OverwriteError on open failure; separately, the custom TTY pristine-state capture/restore around TempStart() overlaps tcell's own Init()/Fini() capture -- dmaluka suggests backporting tcell's Suspend()/Resume() instead but this PR keeps the local capture/restore; maintainers require commits split/squashed per their history preference; merged 2026-04-02 with a follow-up LookPath(sucmd) check to avoid spurious backups when sudo itself is missing

title: Make missing plugin repo errors more informative
note: Merged PR making PluginRepository.Fetch/PluginChannel.Fetch report skipped plugin repos informatively instead of dumping raw JSON-decode errors; settled on using stdlib http.StatusText(resp.StatusCode) for all non-200 statuses (dmaluka) rather than hand-rolled per-code messages, and on returning nil instead of PluginPackages{} everywhere for consistency (JoeKar); related to the still-open #3389 which additionally wants a fetch timeout so a slow/unstable repo host doesn't block other plugins.
